name: Anisotropic Diffusion
desc: Perona-Malik edge-preserving diffusion runs backwards against a drifting noise forcing so structure crystallizes out of static — flat plateaus condense and enlarge while their grain boundaries stay razor-crisp and migrate forever, never settling; rendered as a false-colour micrograph with etched boundaries, an edge-lit radiograph, hatched ink lithography, ironbow thermal, or pure specular chrome relief.

energy.doc: contrast + colour gain of the plateau ramp and the boundary etch (higher = hotter, harder-edged)

scale.doc: magnification into a sub-region of the field — guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: diffusion steps/frame + rate the forcing field drifts (0.2 still evolves)

density.doc: forcing amplitude — how hard fresh noise is injected (low = big calm plateaus, high = turbulent, never consolidates)

kappa.doc: Perona-Malik edge threshold: low = many small regions survive (crisp mosaic), high = everything melts into broad blobs

grain.doc: fixed film-grain tooth on the plateaus + extra boundary etch (texture over flat fill)

hue.doc: primary hue anchoring the palette ramp

x.doc: horizontal pan of the magnified region

y.doc: vertical pan of the magnified region

style.doc: aesthetic: false-colour micrograph / edge-lit radiograph / hatched ink on paper / ironbow thermal / lighting-only chrome relief

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the initial field and the forcing
